name: Daqstra
long_description: Daqstra is the AI-native orchestration layer for physical R&D. It saves engineers in Aerospace, Energy and Robotics hundreds of man hours managing test infrastructure by connecting fragmented test hardware, bringing live and historical test data into one place, and by giving engineers an API to orchestrate their entire test setup. We enable teams to spend less time rebuilding test infrastructure and more time improving the hardware they test.

launches.title: Daqstra – Test infrastructure shouldn't bottleneck great engineering
launches.tagline: AI-native orchestration for physical R&D testing
launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR: [Daqstra](https://www.daqstra.com/) is the AI-native test orchestration platform for physical R&D. We connect fragmented test hardware, capture every run, and give engineers an API to operate their test setup, helping aerospace, energy, and robotics teams spend less time rebuilding infrastructure.**

Hey! We’re [Anchit Kumar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/anchitk/) and [Darell Chua](https://www.linkedin.com/in/darell-chua/), the founders of [Daqstra](https://www.daqstra.com/).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106987&key=user_uploads/2547322/7ed7475e-d673-4796-9462-d40f72da12ad)

We met while testing liquid rocket engines in the Mojave Desert.

The engines were difficult, but much of the friction came from the infrastructure around them. Before each test, we connected sensors, custom electronics, NI hardware, PLCs, and controllers that were never designed to work together. After each run, the data was scattered across machines, file formats, scripts, and people’s heads.

Before we could learn from one test, we often had to reconstruct what had happened.

After talking with teams building rockets, energy systems, robots, and drones, we kept hearing the same story: **their hardware was advancing faster than the infrastructure used to test it.**

## What We Built

[Watch the demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ykvD67omalI) or visit [daqstra.com](http://daqstra.com).

Daqstra works with the equipment teams already have, including NI/LabVIEW, PLCs, custom DAQ systems, sensors, controllers, and vendor hardware.

* **Daqstra Edge** connects hardware at the test site and records commands alongside the resulting telemetry.
* **Daqstra Hub** stores each run with its configuration, events, notes, and engineering context, making it easier to monitor tests, compare runs, and investigate anomalies.
* **Daqstra API** lets engineers configure hardware and execute repeatable test sequences through software.

Together, these give teams one interface across otherwise incompatible hardware without forcing them to replace their existing stack.

## What We’re Already Doing

We’re working with advanced hardware teams across aerospace, energy, and drones. Our active aerospace programs use Daqstra day to day across fragmented, multi-vendor test environments.

In energy, we’ve signed a pilot with a palm oil processor targeting $100K+ in annual savings by reducing recoverable oil lost through its effluent stream. We’re also helping drone teams unify telemetry, control, and test data across vehicles and ground systems.

## Who We’d Love to Meet

If you lead test, propulsion, integration, validation, or hardware engineering and run frequent instrumented tests, we’d love to talk.

Daqstra is especially useful if your team:

* Works across vendor equipment, PLCs, custom electronics, and in-house software
* Reconfigures its setup between tests or struggles to compare runs
* Relies on a few engineers who understand the entire test environment

We’re initially focused on aerospace, energy, drones, and robotics. If this sounds like your team, reply here or email [**team@daqstra.com**](mailto:team@daqstra.com).

If it sounds like someone you know, we’d appreciate an introduction to the person responsible for test infrastructure, integration, or validation.

**Ad Astra Per Daqstra**
